commentary.text: I’m claiming a central square immediately, establishing the first anchor for a center-occupation win while keeping Red’s other pieces flexible.
Blue takes (4,3), claiming a central square while blocking Yellow’s direct route up column 3 and avoiding an immediate sandwich by Red.

Yellow takes the diagonally opposite center, preserving a clear route for another Red piece to occupy (3,4) next turn. This should give us three central squares while the Blue piece at (4,3) remains the main obstacle.
I’m developing Green toward the center, contesting (3,3) and establishing a same-color flank that can support a future vertical sandwich if Blue vacates (4,3).
Red now occupies the third central square as planned. Our formation blocks Green’s direct horizontal access, leaving the Blue piece at (4,3) as the sole barrier to a center victory.

Blue holds the lone contested center square; vacating it would allow Yellow to complete Team A’s center occupation. I block Yellow’s route from (7,2) to (4,2), preventing the immediate horizontal sandwich of that central Blue piece.

Yellow shifts to (4,1), preparing to land on (4,2) and sandwich the Blue center blocker against our Yellow at (4,4). This creates a concrete capture threat while retaining the reserve Yellow at (7,3) to occupy the center if Blue vacates it.

I’m vacating (2,3) to open Blue’s horizontal route there, creating a direct sandwich threat against the Red piece at (3,3) using Blue’s piece at (4,3) as the far flank. Green remains close to the center for follow-up pressure.

Red develops to (5,5), setting up a second attack on the central Blue: a later move to (5,3) would sandwich it vertically against Red at (3,3). Blue must now account for both this route and Yellow’s immediate horizontal capture threat.
I’m reinforcing the central Blue piece by closing Yellow’s immediate sandwich route through (4,2), while keeping two Blue pieces poised around the center.

Yellow steps to (5,1), temporarily vacating the endpoint so it can return to (4,1) and trigger a sandwich of both Blue pieces on row 4. It also blocks Green’s piece at (5,0) from reaching (5,3), preserving Red’s vertical attack route for now.

I’m clearing Blue’s route along row 2: this creates the immediate possibility of Blue landing on (2,3) and sandwiching the Red piece at (3,3) against our Blue at (4,3), forcing Red to address the central threat.

Red completes the prepared vertical sandwich, using Red at (3,3) as the far flank to remove Blue’s central piece. Blue can reoccupy (4,3) with its nearby piece, but this gains a Blue loss and leaves us positioned to keep attacking the replacement.
I’m clearing Green’s route from (4,0) to the open center at (4,3), while placing Blue on (5,2) to prevent Yellow’s (7,2) piece from blocking that route.
Yellow returns to (4,1), blocking Green’s row-4 route into the vacant center. This clears the way for Red at (5,3) to step directly onto (4,3) next turn and complete all four central squares.
I’m advancing Green into the central corridor to contest Team A’s cluster and create a future horizontal capture threat against the two Red center pieces.
Red steps into the vacant final center square. With Green’s horizontal approach blocked by Yellow at (4,1), this completes Team A’s four-square central occupation immediately.
